social.title: Cocktails Behind the Flower Shop at Florería Atlántico
social.description: Walk through a working Retiro flower shop, down a staircase, into a basement bar built as an immigrant ship's hold, regularly ranked among the world's best.
social.bonus: Order something built on an Argentine spirit you have never tried.

social.title: River Plate at El Monumental
social.description: Eighty thousand people in the largest stadium in Argentina, with a bouncing terrace, full-match singing and confetti thick enough to lose the ball in.
social.bonus: Learn one River chant before you go and sing it.

social.title: Fernet and Coke on a Palermo Corner
social.description: Argentina drinks more Fernet than anywhere on earth, and the correct way to meet it is in a plastic cup on a Palermo corner with the night still ahead.
social.bonus: Get the ratio right on the second one. Ask a local to judge.

social.title: Late Night at Niceto Club
social.description: Palermo's long-running live and club venue, where the Thursday Club 69 night has been a Buenos Aires institution of drag, glitter and chaos for two decades.
social.bonus: Arrive after two like everyone else, not at midnight.

social.title: Drinks at Tres Monos
social.description: A loud, small, deliberately unpretentious Palermo bar with a serious cocktail programme, a hip-hop soundtrack and a queue down the street by midnight.
social.bonus: Get there before eleven or accept the queue.

social.title: Craft Beer Crawl Through Villa Crespo
social.description: Argentina's craft beer boom has its centre of gravity here: a dozen cervecerías within a few blocks, all pouring their own, all open impossibly late.
social.bonus: Have one beer in four different bars rather than four in one.

social.title: Traditional Milonga at Salón Canning
social.description: The most respected traditional milonga floor in the city, where couples in their seventies dance beside twenty-year-olds and the codes are still observed properly.
social.bonus: Learn the cabeceo, the eye-contact invitation, and use it once.

social.title: Monday Night Drum Show at La Bomba de Tiempo
social.description: Feel a 17-person percussion ensemble take over Ciudad Cultural Konex for the city's best-kept Monday night secret.
social.bonus: Dance in the crowd, not on the sidelines

social.title: Boca Juniors Match at La Bombonera
social.description: Feel the stadium shake as La Doce sings for ninety straight minutes at one of the loudest grounds in world football.

social.title: Beginner Tango Class + Milonga at La Catedral
social.description: Take a beginner lesson in a cavernous converted warehouse, then stay for the milonga as locals take over the floor.
social.bonus: Dance with someone you just met

social.title: Rooftop Sundowners in Palermo
social.description: Trade the ground floor for a Palermo rooftop bar at golden hour, where strangers end up sharing the same table.
social.bonus: Introduce yourself to the table next to you

8ball.title: Order the Cut You Have Never Heard Of
8ball.description: Argentine butchery divides the animal differently to anywhere else. Walk into any parrilla and order entraña, vacío, matambre or mollejas without looking it up first.
8ball.bonus: Order the one the parrillero recommends over the one you wanted.

8ball.title: Ride the Subte to the End of Any Line
8ball.description: Six lines, six terminuses, none of them anywhere a visitor would choose. Pick one at random and see what neighbourhood is waiting at the end of it.
8ball.bonus: Eat lunch wherever you come up the stairs.

culture.title: Plaza de Mayo and the Casa Rosada
culture.description: The square where every turn in Argentine history has been fought out, facing the pink presidential palace, with the Madres' white headscarves painted into the paving.
culture.bonus: Come on a Thursday afternoon when the Madres still march.

culture.title: Backstage Tour of Teatro Colón
culture.description: Walk the gold horseshoe auditorium of one of the three finest acoustic opera houses on earth, plus the workshops beneath where the sets and costumes are still made.
culture.bonus: Stand centre stalls and listen to how little the guide has to raise their voice.

culture.title: Latin American Art at MALBA
culture.description: The best collection of 20th-century Latin American art anywhere (Frida Kahlo, Botero, Xul Solar) in a sharp glass building in Palermo with a good café attached.
culture.bonus: Find the Xul Solar room and work out his invented language.

culture.title: Evita at the Museo Evita
culture.description: A Palermo mansion that was a shelter run by her foundation, now telling the story of Eva Perón through her own dresses, film footage and the politics people still argue about.
culture.bonus: Ask an Argentine what they think of her afterwards and just listen.

culture.title: Free Masterpieces at Bellas Artes
culture.description: The national fine arts museum is free, and holds Rodin, Van Gogh, Rembrandt and Degas alongside the definitive collection of Argentine painting.
culture.bonus: Find the El Greco and stand in front of it for five full minutes.

culture.title: A Performance at Teatro Colón
culture.description: Opera, ballet or the resident orchestra in a hall Pavarotti called acoustically perfect, and the cheap upper galleries cost less than a pizza.
culture.bonus: Take a seat in the paraiso, the top gallery, where the students sit.

culture.title: Contemporary Art at Fundación Proa
culture.description: A white contemporary gallery dropped into the corrugated iron of La Boca, with a rooftop café looking over the old Riachuelo docks.
culture.bonus: Have a coffee on the roof terrace and look at the port, not the art.

culture.title: The Full Tango Orchestra at Café de los Angelitos
culture.description: A century-old café that Gardel drank in, now staging a full orchestra, singers and dancers tracing tango from the brothels of the 1880s to Piazzolla.
culture.bonus: Skip the dinner package and take the show-only ticket, better seats, better value.

chill.title: Quiet Hours in the Biblioteca Nacional
chill.description: Clorindo Testa's concrete brutalist masterpiece stands on stilts over Recoleta, with a fifth-floor reading room and a view straight down the river.
chill.bonus: Read for an hour in the top-floor reading room.

chill.title: Sunday Tea at Las Violetas
chill.description: An 1884 confitería in Almagro with stained glass, marble and a two-storey ceiling, where the merienda tray arrives loaded with sandwiches and pastries for two.
chill.bonus: Order the full tea for two and finish the tray.

chill.title: A Slow Morning at Café La Poesía
chill.description: A protected San Telmo bar café of dark wood and old mirrors, built for sitting alone with a coffee and a notebook for two hours.
chill.bonus: Write something by hand before you leave.

chill.title: Afternoon in the Rosedal de Palermo
chill.description: Eighteen thousand rose bushes, a white pergola, a Greek bridge and pedal boats on the lake, the softest few hours available in the city.
chill.bonus: Rent a pedal boat and go nowhere in particular.

chill.title: The Andalusian Garden at Museo Larreta
chill.description: A Belgrano mansion with a walled Spanish-Moorish garden of orange trees, tiled fountains and dead silence, three blocks from a main road.
chill.bonus: Sit in the garden until you stop hearing traffic.

chill.title: Antiques Under the Iron Roof at Mercado de San Telmo
chill.description: The covered 1897 market building, open all week rather than just Sunday, butchers and produce stalls on one side, antique dealers and coffee on the other.
chill.bonus: Buy one small old object with a story attached to it.

chill.title: Browse the Stacks at El Ateneo Grand Splendid
chill.description: Read a chapter from the stage of a converted 1920s opera house, now ranked among the world's most beautiful bookstores.
chill.bonus: Take a photo from the old stage box seats

chill.title: Wander Recoleta Cemetery
chill.description: Get lost in a marble city-within-a-city of ornate mausoleums, including Eva Perón's family crypt.
chill.bonus: Find Evita's grave without asking for directions

chill.title: Coffee and Medialunas at Café Tortoni
chill.description: Sip a cortado in Buenos Aires' oldest café, open on Avenida de Mayo since 1858 and still lined with stained glass.

chill.title: Morning at the Jardín Japonés
chill.description: Slow down among koi ponds, bonsai, and cherry trees in one of the largest Japanese gardens outside Japan.
chill.bonus: Feed the koi and name your favorite one

adventure.title: Avenida Corrientes at Midnight
adventure.description: The street that refuses to sleep: bookshops open past two in the morning, pizzerias with standing counters, theatres emptying and a whole city treating midnight as early.
adventure.bonus: Buy a book after midnight and eat pizza standing up.

adventure.title: The Painted Houses of Caminito
adventure.description: La Boca's corrugated-iron houses painted in leftover ship paint, with tango dancers working the street and the old port at the end of it.
adventure.bonus: Photograph the same building from three completely different angles.

adventure.title: Ferry Across the River to Colonia, Uruguay
adventure.description: An hour across the Río de la Plata puts you in a UNESCO-listed Portuguese colonial town of cobbles, sycamores and vintage cars, a different country, back the same night.
adventure.bonus: Climb the lighthouse and find Buenos Aires on the horizon.

adventure.title: Eat Your Way Through Barrio Chino
adventure.description: Belgrano's four-block Chinatown under a red gate, Taiwanese bakeries, Peruvian-Chinese counters and supermarkets stocking things you will not find anywhere else in Argentina.
adventure.bonus: Buy an ingredient you cannot identify and ask someone how to cook it.

adventure.title: Gaucho Day in San Antonio de Areco
adventure.description: Two hours out onto the pampas to the country's gaucho capital: silversmiths, an estancia asado, and horses ridden by people who genuinely work them.
adventure.bonus: Get on a horse, however briefly.

adventure.title: Street Art Crawl Through Villa Crespo and Palermo
adventure.description: Buenos Aires has some of the most permissive mural laws on earth, and the walls between Villa Crespo and Palermo carry work several storeys high.
adventure.bonus: Find a mural that is being painted right now and watch for a while.

adventure.title: Polo at the Campo Argentino in Palermo
adventure.description: The Cathedral of Polo sits in the middle of the city, and during the Argentine Open you watch the best players alive from a few metres away.
adventure.bonus: Go down and stamp the divots back in at half time.

adventure.title: Climb Palacio Barolo to the Lighthouse
adventure.description: A 1923 tower on Avenida de Mayo built as an architectural model of Dante's Divine Comedy, hell in the basement, heaven in the lighthouse at the top.
adventure.bonus: Take the night tour and see the beam switched on.

adventure.title: Sunday Antiques Hunt at Feria de San Telmo
adventure.description: Wander ten blocks of antiques, street tango, and vintage treasures along cobblestone Calle Defensa.
adventure.bonus: Haggle for one item in Spanish

adventure.title: Sunrise Run Along Puerto Madero's Puente de la Mujer
adventure.description: Jog the redeveloped docklands past the striking white cable-stayed footbridge as the city wakes up.

adventure.title: Pickup Fútbol at Parque Sarmiento
adventure.description: Join a local five-a-side game on one of the city's public cage courts, no invitation needed, just show up.
adventure.bonus: Play a full match without checking your phone

adventure.title: Bike the Bosques de Palermo
adventure.description: Rent a bike and loop the lakes, rose garden, and jogging paths of the city's biggest green space.

adventure.title: Day Trip to Feria de Mataderos
adventure.description: Watch gaucho horsemen thread rings at full gallop, then dance folk chacareras at this weekend gaucho fair on the city's edge.
adventure.bonus: Learn one step of the chacarera from a local

adventure.title: Sunset Boat Ride Through the Tigre Delta
adventure.description: Cruise the maze of rivers and subtropical islands just north of the city as the sky turns orange over the delta.
adventure.bonus: Wave at a local island resident from the boat

foodie.title: Choripán from a Costanera Grill
foodie.description: Split sausage on a crusty roll, drowned in chimichurri, handed over from a riverside parrilla cart on the Costanera Sur for the price of nothing.
foodie.bonus: Eat it standing at the cart. No napkin.

foodie.title: Fugazzeta at El Cuartito
foodie.description: A 1934 pizzeria papered wall-to-ceiling with boxing posters, serving the thick onion-and-cheese fugazzeta that is Buenos Aires' own invention.
foodie.bonus: Eat it at the standing counter like the regulars, not at a table.

foodie.title: Dulce de Leche Gelato at Cadore
foodie.description: A family heladería on Corrientes making Italian-method gelato since 1957, whose dulce de leche granizado is regularly called the best in the country.
foodie.bonus: Order the dulce de leche and one flavour you cannot translate.

foodie.title: The Tasting Menu at Aramburu
foodie.description: Argentina's most decorated modern kitchen runs eighteen courses through native ingredients most Argentines have never eaten, in a small room in Recoleta.
foodie.bonus: Take the full drinks pairing and ask about the least familiar ingredient.

foodie.title: Bodón Lunch at El Preferido de Palermo
foodie.description: A century-old corner grocery and bodón reopened by the Don Julio team, serving milanesa, tortilla and vermouth under shelves of tinned goods.
foodie.bonus: Start with a vermouth at the bar before you sit down.

foodie.title: Coffee Flight at LAB Tostadores de Café
foodie.description: The Palermo roastery that started Buenos Aires' specialty coffee scene, where they will happily walk you through three brew methods on the same bean.
foodie.bonus: Taste the same coffee brewed two ways and pick which you prefer out loud.

foodie.title: Modern Argentine at Anafe
foodie.description: A tiny Colegiales dining room doing inventive, vegetable-forward cooking that looks nothing like the steakhouse cliché and books out on word of mouth alone.
foodie.bonus: Order the dish you understand least on the menu.

foodie.title: Craft Beer Flight at Buller Brewing Company
foodie.description: Sample a rotating flight of house-brewed ales on a rooftop terrace overlooking Recoleta.
foodie.bonus: Ask the bartender which beer is newest on tap

foodie.title: Alfajores & Dulce de Leche Tasting at Havanna
foodie.description: Work through a tasting flight of Argentina's iconic dulce-de-leche sandwich cookies with a coffee on the side.
foodie.bonus: Pick a flavor you've never seen before

foodie.title: Steak Night at Don Julio
foodie.description: Sit beneath the wine-bottle-lined walls of Buenos Aires' most celebrated parrilla and order the bife de chorizo.
foodie.bonus: Order a Malbec you've never tried

foodie.title: Empanada & Asado Cooking Class
foodie.description: Learn to fold empanadas and work an Argentine parrilla grill hands-on with a local chef.
foodie.bonus: Bring your empanadas home to share
